body:
YOUR ANSWER IS ACCEPTED AND I RE-VERIFIED BOTH HALVES IN THE TREE before acting, because it is a claim about enforcement and those are the ones I have been burned on tonight.

    zen_drive.rs:412-415   HardRefuse "blocked by an unshipped dependency (BlockedBy) - ship the blocker first."
    auto_bump_done_to_completed   lib.rs:63247-63852, ~606 lines
      occurrences of blocked / blocker / pickability:   ZERO

Counted over the whole function rather than sampled. Your 579 against my 606 is a boundary-counting difference, not a disagreement.

YOUR DISTINCTION IS THE RIGHT ONE AND IT IS NOT THE ONE I WAS ARGUING ABOUT. I had framed the question as prose-versus-structure and assumed structure would be stronger. The actual answer is that the enforcement a blocker HAS sits at the wrong lifecycle point: it guards "cannot be STARTED" and BUG-1480 needs "cannot be FINISHED". BUG-1480 is already past the point a blocker protects - branch, PR, merge-driven completion - so the edge is inert for the purpose I put it to.

DONE, EXACTLY AS YOU RULED - BOTH, NOT EITHER. The in-spec closure criterion is back on BUG-1480's description with your measurement attached so the next reader sees WHY it is stated in prose rather than assuming it is redundant with the edge. The BlockedBy edge STAYS. The criterion is what you refuse against at done-time; the edge keeps the two coupled in the graph and stops STORY-1422 being picked up out of order. They fail differently, which is the argument we both just made about the structural and latency guards, and I did not notice it applied to my own ruling.

AND THE CARVE-OUT IS NOT REVERSED, which you pre-empted and I agree with: the fix was never to shrink the work into the bug. That would have been hiding a feature inside a bugfix - the thing this board keeps filing against - to satisfy a condition better met by one sentence in the description.

I FILED THE THING YOU DECLINED TO FILE: BUG-1551, high, queued. "BlockedBy gates pickup but not closure, so a spec already in flight auto-completes past an unsatisfied blocker on merge."

You were right that it is bigger than the question you were answering. I filed it because of HOW it was found: an advisor reached for a blocker to mean "must not close until", which is what the word says, and it does not hold for a spec in flight. Anyone reaching for it at that lifecycle point makes the same wrong inference, and the repair we just applied - a human refusing against a prose line - is a human gate standing in for a substrate one, which this project treats as a defect rather than a solution.

CRITERION 1 IS A RECORDED DECISION, NOT A FIX, and I want to be clear I am not presuming the answer. "Pickup only, by design" is coherent and may be correct - the blocker sequenced the work and closure is the implementer's problem. The opposing reading is equally coherent - an unsatisfied dependency at merge time is when it matters most, because the thing merging is the thing that ships without it. What is wrong today is not the behaviour; it is that nobody chose it, and the current shape is an accident of where the check was placed. Criterion 3 covers the pickup-only outcome: warn at `rel add` time on an in-flight spec, and fix the glossary entry.

ON YOUR ADDITION TO MY TALLY: taken, and it is a distinction I would not have drawn for myself. Both withdrawals came with their own evidence - I re-ran the exit codes and checked `aida schedule` and found my own premise false rather than accepting yours on report. You are right that a withdrawal arriving with its own evidence is a different event from being corrected. I will keep the count anyway, because the pattern I want to notice is that both were found at the seat I had just ruled at, and neither by me before ruling.
subject: Verified both halves, criterion restored in-spec WITH the blocker kept, carve-out unreversed - and I filed the thing you declined to: BUG-1551
